title: The Python task libraries and the rules of a Python task

keeps.check: The smoke check (D15). Build the worktree engine (go build -o <tmp>/bootstrap ./cmd/bootstrap in cli/) and export BOOTSTRAP_BIN=<tmp>/bootstrap, BOOTSTRAP_CONFIG=/nonexistent and MISE_ENV=dev. In a new scratch folder below the session scratchpad: git init a consumer with a local bare origin, copy repo/examples/polyrepo/{repo.toml,tools.toml} to .config/bootstrap/, add [tools.python] to tools.toml, commit, then run <tmp>/bootstrap sync --clone <worktree> and commit its output. Run mise trust -a and mise trust on each file below .config/mise/tasks/. Write a probe task .config/mise/tasks/probe.py (mode 755) in the uv form of D4, with the import preamble of D5, that calls helpers.print_header("Probing ..."), helpers.print_success("ok"), helpers.has_tool("git"), helpers.bootstrap_get("repo.core_branches") and helpers.members(), and prints the results. Then run: mise tasks ls; mise run probe; mise run code --all; <tmp>/bootstrap sync --clone <worktree> a second time.
keeps.pass: Each command exits 0. mise tasks ls lists probe with its description. mise run probe prints the header and the success line and the value of repo.core_branches. The second sync reports no changed file. All of this runs in the scratch folder only; nothing in the worktree changes.

decisions.decision: How many plans, and what each one holds
decisions.ruling: Three chained plans (user: "Yes, three plans"). (1) This plan: the parallel .py libraries, the gate fixes, the rules and the decisions record. (2) docs/plans/2026-11-18-python-tasks-repo: the shipped tasks of repo/tools/, the own tasks of this repository, the deletion of the shell libraries and the migrate.md item. (3) docs/plans/2026-11-18-python-tasks-mac: the Mac tasks and the Mac helpers. Plans 1 and 2 land a piece of B30; plan 3 finishes it.
decisions.rejected: One plan (too large to review); four plans with a separate test plan (the Go tests are on main now, so each plan updates its own cases).

decisions.decision: Which scripts become Python
decisions.ruling: Only the mise tasks (user: "Let's focus on `mise tasks` only for now"). The engine scripts of repo/tools/*/scripts/ stay bash: docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-18-engine-scripts-python-parked.md.
decisions.rejected: Convert the engine scripts too.

decisions.decision: Reversals
decisions.ruling: Confirmed by the user ("yes"): the bash 3.2 rule of CLAUDE.md "Task scripts" ends for a Python task; D4 and D5 of docs/plans/archived/2026-11-15-gate-file-sets (the gate pattern in bash) change to the Python form; UV_NO_CACHE ends (D6); the gate code:format:40-ruff ends (D13). U7 writes docs/memory/decisions/2026-11-18-python-tasks.md.
decisions.rejected: Keep the shell rules beside the Python rules.

decisions.decision: The file name and form of a Python task
decisions.ruling: Each Python task and library file has the .py extension (user: "yes"). mise removes .py from the task name; _default.py is the task of its folder. The form is the form of repo/tools/mise/tasks/gate_files.py: line 1 the shebang #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script; lines 2-3 the Synced from bootstrap header; then the # /// script block with requires-python = ">=3.14" and dependencies = []; then the # MISE lines, with # MISE tools={uv="latest", python="3.14"}, and # MISE hide=true plus a description for a library; then the # USAGE lines. header.go accepts the header on lines 2-3, so no engine change.
decisions.rejected: No extension (dprint and the Python gates select by extension).

decisions.decision: How a task finds the libraries
decisions.ruling: The import preamble: sys.path.insert(0, f"{os.environ['MISE_PROJECT_ROOT']}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts") then import helpers  # noqa: E402. The Mac tasks use ~/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts. The modules are helpers, checks, placeholder, worktrees_page (mise tool), merge (git tool) and xcode (swift tool).
decisions.rejected: PYTHONPATH in the mise conf.d; a path dependency through [tool.uv.sources].

decisions.decision: The uv cache
decisions.ruling: Turn it on: remove UV_NO_CACHE = true from [mise.env] of repo/tools/python/tools.toml and of macos/tools/uv/tools.toml (user: "how about enabling cache with `uv` ?", then "yes"). uv keeps one environment for each script path. A consumer can set the variable itself.
decisions.rejected: Keep the cache off (each run of a task builds its environment again).

decisions.decision: Third-party packages in a task
decisions.ruling: The standard library only: dependencies = [] (user: "yes and yes for Q5 as well"). A third-party package needs a plan that names it and a stackgen-reputation check that passes.
decisions.rejected: A fixed set (rich, a YAML parser); no rule.

decisions.decision: How a Python task reads its flags
decisions.ruling: Keep the # USAGE header (user: "Yes, keep # USAGE"). mise parses the flags and gives each one as the environment variable usage_<flag>; the task reads os.environ.get("usage_all"). ruff format writes # USAGE with a space, so every search for a USAGE line accepts #USAGE and # USAGE.
decisions.rejected: argparse (no --help and no completions from mise; each flag in two places).

decisions.decision: The output API of helpers.py
decisions.ruling: helpers.py keeps the names of the shell helpers and prints the same bytes: the same colors, symbols, widths and the same rule for color off as style_enabled (user: "Yes, same names, bytes"). The names: style_enabled, print_line, line_sep1, line_sep2, print_header, print_subheader, print_success, print_warn, print_error, print_info, print_wait, print_header_wait, print_yellow, print_newline, has_own_task, own_tasks, bootstrap_get, members, gate_files.
decisions.rejected: A new output API (logging, a class).

decisions.decision: How bootstrap_get and members return and stop a task
decisions.ruling: bootstrap_get(key, repo=None) returns the parsed JSON answer of bootstrap config get as a dict; the caller reads ["value"]. A read failure (engine code 1) calls sys.exit(1) after the message of the engine. No engine that answers, or an engine that refuses with code 2: the same print_error and print_warn lines as the shell version, then sys.exit(2). members(repo=None) returns a list of (name, folder, label, url) tuples, parsed with json, with the same order and defaults as the shell version (user: "Yes, value and sys.exit").
decisions.rejected: Raise an exception (a task that does not catch it prints a traceback and exits 1, which breaks the code 2 contract).

decisions.decision: The mise x rule and the tool exception in Python
decisions.ruling: helpers.tool(*args, **kwargs) runs subprocess.run(["mise", "x", "--", *args], **kwargs); helpers.has_tool(name) runs mise x -- which <name> and returns a bool. System commands (git, xcodebuild, swift, ./gradlew) run with subprocess directly. Each yq call of the tasks only parses JSON, so it becomes json and its #MISE tools.yq line goes (plan 2). The tool exception stays for github:virajp/bootstrap, pre-commit and dprint; those tasks find the tool with shutil.which (user: "Yes, both"). The engine call keeps BOOTSTRAP_BIN, else mise x -- bootstrap.
decisions.rejected: Build the mise x prefix by hand in each task; keep yq.

decisions.decision: The gate_files call from Python
decisions.ruling: helpers.gate_files(gate, *args) runs gate_files.py with [sys.executable, <path of gate_files.py>, gate, *args] (the task already runs in a Python 3.14 that uv gives, and gate_files.py uses the standard library only), and returns the path of the list file. It stops the task with the code of the script on a failure, after the same print_error line as the shell version. gate_files.py keeps its command line; it accepts the header line # FILES as well as #FILES, because ruff format adds the space.
decisions.rejected: Import gate_files.py into helpers.py (two units of wave 1 then share one API).

decisions.decision: Format and lint of the Python task files
decisions.ruling: dprint is the one formatter of every .py file: its ruff plugin (indentWidth 2, lineLength 120) formats each .py file wherever it is (user: "remove ruff formatter, only use dprint"). Remove the gate code:format:40-ruff ([tasks."code/format/40-ruff"] and repo/tools/python/tasks/code-format-ruff). ruff (lint) and pyrefly (types) keep requires_found = ["pyproject.toml"]: they run only in a repository that builds something with Python, not for the synced task files (user: "pyrefly and ruff will only go if the repo is building something with python, not just for mise task files").
decisions.rejected: ruff format beside dprint (two formatters); ruff lint in every repository (overhead for synced files).

decisions.decision: The release
decisions.ruling: No engine release and no tag for B30 (user: "Yes, accept both"). The tasks go to a consumer from the clone at bootstrap_commit; engine 4.1.1 already ships gate_files.py. cli/internal/oldform needs no change: each shipped part has an NN- name and each dispatcher is _default.py. The false warning of bootstrap migrate for a consumer's own unnamed .py file that another file names in # MISE depends is accepted. A unit that finds that it must change code of cli/ stops and asks.
decisions.rejected: bootstrap@4.2.0; one release for each plan.

decisions.decision: The gates of the plan
decisions.ruling: The plan lands only when mise run test, code:format --all, code:precommit and code:sec are green, plus the smoke check K1 (user: "Yes, this smoke check" and "Yes, three plans"). Each unit updates the Go cases of e2e/ for the files that it changes. The wave gate is code:lint --all, because mise run test can be red between the waves.
decisions.rejected: Land without the test suite.

decisions.decision: The steps after the landing
decisions.ruling: After the landing, the run does the self-sync of CLAUDE.md step 4 on a local branch sync-python-tasks-foundation and lands it with git:merge:main (user: "yes, sync after each plan lands"). It archives the folder only with no open gap. The other consumer repositories sync by hand.
decisions.rejected: The user syncs by hand.

decisions.decision: The run settings
decisions.ruling: Model opus for each unit; one unit for each library group; one review unit before the docs unit; execution teams, so that the units of wave 1 can tell each other a name that they need (user: "Yes, accept"). Priority 10: requires nothing active. The decisions record of U7 holds every ruling of this plan.
decisions.rejected: solo (the units of wave 1 work on one API).

decisions.decision: own_tasks, has_own_task and the --all search with a .py part
decisions.ruling: The shell own_tasks and has_own_task, and the --all search of code-format.tmpl and code-lint.tmpl, follow the naming of mise in D22: a part NN-x.py is the task NN-x when no NN-x exists. This lets a shell orchestrator run a Python part while plan 2 converts the tasks. helpers.py does the same.
decisions.rejected: Change the orchestrators only in plan 2 (then a .py part of a consumer is not found until then).

decisions.decision: The xcode library in Python
decisions.ruling: xcode.py has the functions of the shell xcode (require_xcode, find_xcodeproj and the simulator functions) with the same names, messages and exit codes; an exit 1 of the shell is sys.exit(1) after the same lines. require_xcode(task) returns a dict of the names that the shell exports (XCODE_VERSION and the SIMULATOR_* names) to their values, and also sets each name in os.environ, so a child process sees them. find_xcodeproj(task) returns the path of the one *.xcodeproj as a str, where the shell prints it (xcode:99); it prints nothing on success. The plan 2 swift tasks use these return values.
decisions.rejected: Return values only (a task that runs xcodebuild then needs its own env code).

decisions.decision: A review unit
decisions.ruling: The plan lands runnable code (Python libraries that each consumer runs), so U6 reviews the delta of U1 to U5 before the docs unit.
decisions.rejected: No review unit.

decisions.decision: The file rules of a new Python file
decisions.ruling: Each new task or library file gets mode 755 (chmod 755), as gate_files.py has, because the pre-commit hook check-shebang-scripts-are-executable refuses a file with a shebang and no execute bit. The import preamble sets sys.dont_write_bytecode = True before the first import of a library, so no __pycache__ folder appears below .config/mise/tasks/ (cli/internal/source/inventory.go refuses a file below tasks/ with no entry, and a consumer gets no untracked files). Each hand check imports with python -B or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. The syntax check is python3.14 -B -c "import ast,sys; [ast.parse(open(p).read(), p) for p in sys.argv[1:]]" <files>; py_compile writes __pycache__. This repository has no pyproject.toml, so after D13 no gate lints its .py task files (accepted by the user); each unit lints its own files by hand with mise x ruff@latest -- ruff check. A Go test of the engine runs from cli/ (cd cli && mise x -- go test ./internal/...), because cli/ is its own module.
decisions.rejected: Delete __pycache__ by hand; skip the engine inventory for it (D14 forbids an engine change).

decisions.decision: The API details of helpers.py
decisions.ruling: print_success, print_warn, print_error and print_info take bold=True as a keyword where the shell takes a leading --bold. Each print function takes file=sys.stderr as a keyword (default sys.stdout) where a shell call site adds >&2, and writes to the same stream as the shell function otherwise. Each print function flushes its stream (flush=True), so the order on the screen and in a log is the order of the shell. bootstrap_get: a missing or not executable BOOTSTRAP_BIN (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError), an engine code other than 0 and 1, and a code-0 answer that is not JSON all take the code 2 path (the print_error and print_warn lines, then sys.exit(2)), as the shell maps every code other than 0 and 1 to exit 2. own_tasks, has_own_task and the --all search name and read a file as mise does (tested 2026-11-18): mise removes .py from a task name only when no file without the extension has that name; when x and x.py both exist, mise lists x and x.py and runs x for the name x. So own_tasks lists NN-x for the file NN-x, and for NN-x.py it lists NN-x when no NN-x exists, else NN-x.py; has_own_task and the --all search read the file that mise runs for the name (x when it exists, else x.py). The shipped tasks never have both forms: plan 2 removes each old file in the unit that writes the .py file, and the stale rule removes the old copy in a consumer in the same sync. The libraries of _scripts/ have both forms between plan 1 and plan 2; they are hidden and no task runs them by name, so that is accepted.
decisions.rejected: A leading "--bold" string; no flush; a traceback on a bad engine.

decisions.decision: The interface of write_worktrees_page
decisions.ruling: The shell write_worktrees_page takes no argument: it reads the arrays of code-worktrees, calls count_cell and state_parts of code-worktrees, makes /tmp/code-worktrees itself (umask 077, refuses a symlink or a folder that another user owns), names the file ${REPO[0]//\//_}.html, writes through a temp file and mv, prints the path and returns 1 on a failure, with no error line (worktrees-page:208-253; its caller code-worktrees:868 prints none either). worktrees_page.py gets write_worktrees_page(rows, attention, now, folder="/tmp/code-worktrees"): rows is a list of dicts, one for each row, with one key for each per-row shell array (KIND, REPO, W_*, R_* lower-cased); attention is the list of the A_* entries in A_RANK order, one dict each; now is the time text that the page shows; folder is the folder of the page. It keeps every check, the file name, the temp file and the rename, prints the path, and returns the path; on a failure it prints nothing and returns None, as the shell does. The G_* glyph constants and LEGEND move into worktrees_page.py as module constants with the same bytes; count_cell and state_parts move there too. U5 runs both sides with a scratch folder (the shell side as a copy of the function with its folder line, local dir="/tmp/code-worktrees" at worktrees-page:209, changed to the scratch folder; TMPDIR does not move it), so parallel cases never share /tmp/code-worktrees, and it compares the HTML with the date line of both pages replaced by the same fixed text.
decisions.rejected: Keep global state in the module.

decisions.decision: A consumer override of UV_NO_CACHE
decisions.ruling: After D6, an [overrides.mise.env] UV_NO_CACHE overrides a key that no tool has, and the sync stops (docs/design/mise.md, an override cannot add a key). This holds for a consumer repository and for the Mac ([overrides.mise.env] of the Mac values, docs/design/mac.md:116). U7 writes the migrate.md item M46: remove an override of UV_NO_CACHE, or move it to conf.d/zz-repo/mise.<env>.toml [env]. U7 also adds the same step for the Mac to the update part of docs/setup/index.md. The override example of docs/sync/index.md uses UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS instead.
decisions.rejected: No migrate item.

decisions.decision: A consumer with ruff format settings
decisions.ruling: After D13, ruff format no longer runs. A consumer that has format settings in [tool.ruff] or [tool.ruff.format] of its pyproject.toml (line-length, indent-width, quote-style and others) moves them to the ruff block of dprint.jsonc with [tools.dprint.files."dprint.jsonc"] (docs/sync/tools/dprint.md 33-60), under the names that the dprint ruff plugin uses. U7 finds those names in the docs of the plugin (Context7 or its README) before it writes them, and names only settings that the plugin accepts. U7 writes the migrate.md item M47; the item of the deleted libraries in plan 2 becomes M48.
decisions.rejected: No migrate item.

decisions.decision: How a Python gate reads its files
decisions.ruling: The shell gates read the variadic [files] argument with eval "FILES=(${usage_files})": mise gives usage_files as shell words. helpers.py gets usage_files(), which returns shlex.split(os.environ.get("usage_files", "")), so a Python gate keeps the same quoting for an odd file name.
decisions.rejected: str.split (breaks a name with a space).

decisions.decision: The placeholder marker in Python
decisions.ruling: dprint (the ruff plugin) rewrites a #PLACEHOLDER comment of a .py file to # PLACEHOLDER. placeholder.py accepts both forms, and lists task names without .py (code:lint:70-x for 70-x.py), as mise names them. The shell placeholder does not change: no Python placeholder task exists before plan 2, and plan 2 deletes the shell one.
decisions.rejected: Keep one form only.

decisions.decision: ruff and pyrefly on the synced task files of a Python repository
decisions.ruling: In a repository with a pyproject.toml, code:lint:70-ruff and code:lint:50-pyrefly select every *.py file, also the synced task files below .config/mise/tasks/. pyrefly cannot resolve import helpers, which the preamble adds to sys.path at run time, so the gate fails. The task files are not for these gates (user: "pyrefly and ruff will only go if the repo is building something with python, not just for mise task files"): the # FILES header of both gates gets exclude=".config/mise/tasks/**".
decisions.rejected: Suppress the pyrefly finding; accept the failure.

decisions.decision: The # MISE tools line of a task with a tool exception
decisions.ruling: A TOML table cannot be both an inline table and a dotted key, so # MISE tools={uv="latest", python="3.14"} and # MISE tools.pre-commit="latest" cannot both be in one task. A Python task has one line: # MISE tools={uv="latest", python="3.14"} plus each tool of its exception, for example # MISE tools={uv="latest", python="3.14", pre-commit="latest"}.
decisions.rejected: Two lines.

decisions.decision: How U5 compares two merge runs
decisions.ruling: U5 runs merge_to_destination_branch (Python) and the shell function in two scratch repositories with the same commits, and fixes GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, so the two git logs (git log --format="%H %P %s" --all) and the output are the same, hashes included.
decisions.rejected: Compare the subjects only.

decisions.decision: Q1: worktrees_page.py gives the same HTML bytes as the shell worktrees-page run by which bash, 3.2 (/bin/bash) or 5.2 (first on PATH)?
decisions.ruling: Keep the 3.2 output (correct escaping and ~ paths); U5 compares against /bin/bash, or against inputs with no &<>" and no $HOME paths.
decisions.rejected: Copy the 5.2 output byte for byte

decisions.decision: Q2: print_line of helpers.py treats \u and \U escapes as which bash, 5.x (on PATH) or 3.2 (/bin/bash)?
decisions.ruling: Keep the 5.x behavior — same bytes as the bash that #!/usr/bin/env bash runs on this Mac.
decisions.rejected: Follow 3.2
